units: <cite ref="Niddah 4b:15">Nidd. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>ה׳ על מדותיו</he> went beyond his measures, i.e. extended the restrictions of the law too far.

<cite ref="Nedarim 32a:15">Ned. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>ה׳ על מדותיו של הקב״ה</he> he went too far in testing the attributes (goodness) of the Lord, i.e. presumed on God’s kindness by asking for a sign (<cite ref="Genesis 15:8">Gen. XV, 8</cite>); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 74">Yalk. Gen. 74</cite>.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 8:8">Koh. R. to VIII, 8</cite> <he>מַפְרִיזִין באצבעותיהן וכ׳</he> pointed with their fingers towards a distance, saying, the vision which he sees &c. (<cite ref="Ezekiel 12:27">Ez. XII, 27</cite>); (Lam. R. introd. (R. Ḥan. 1) <he>ומורין</he>, v. <cite ref="J00601"><he>יָרָה</he></cite>).

senses.gloss: to offer a higher rent than originally stipulated in consideration of a loan to be used to improve the property.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 5:5">B. Mets. V, 5</cite> <he>ומַפְרִיז על שדהו וכ׳</he> (Var. <he>ומַפְרִין</he>; Ms. M. <he>ומפרי׳</he>; Y. ed. <he>ומפרין</he>) and a tenant may offer higher rent for his field in consideration of a loan for improvements, and need not regard the appearance of usury. Ib. 69ᵇ <he>אין מפריז לא על חנות וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. everywhere <he>מפרין</he>) you dare not offer higher rent for a shop or a ship in consideration of a loan (to be invested in the business); Y. ib. V, 10ᶜ top <he>מפרין</he>; v. <cite ref="Q01783"><he>פָּרָה</he></cite> a. <cite ref="Q01879"><he>פָּרַן</he></cite>.
